used_for: sign-in (user access token: identity and installation binding only)
repository access for pinned snapshot fetches
pushing a new migration branch and opening a pull request, only on repositories where the consumer authorized migration PRs

reasons: GitHub enforces the split: an installation token 'cannot be granted permissions that the app was not granted', so no Reader token can ever write, whatever Shockwave's database says (installation-access-token).

The write scope is chosen in GitHub by the installer: the PR Writer is installed with 'Only select repositories' on exactly the repositories where migration PRs are authorized, while permissions are per installation, so one upgraded app would hold write access on every repository selected for analysis (install-selected-repositories).

Adding permissions to one app asks every installation to approve them and, until approved, the installation keeps its old permissions, so analysis-only consumers would face a write request they never asked for (permission-change-approval, approve-updated-permissions).

Revoking PR writes is a GitHub-native, observable action (uninstall the PR Writer or remove a repository from it; installation and installation_repositories webhooks are delivered by default) that leaves read access and analysis untouched (webhook-installation, webhook-installation-repositories).
apps.rejected_alternative: One app upgraded to contents:write + pull_requests:write plus a Shockwave-side per-repository PR flag: one install and one key pair, but write capability would exist on every selected repository and the per-repository restriction would live only in Shockwave (narrowing tokens with repository_ids and permissions helps, but is still enforced only by Shockwave).
tradeoffs: Two app registrations: two private keys and two webhook secrets to manage, and two installation steps for the consumer.

Installing the PR Writer needs the account owner, an organization owner, or a repository admin for repositories they administer (neither app requests organization permissions) (install-selected-repositories).

contents:write covers every branch of an installed repository; 'never push to the default branch, never force-push, never merge' is Shockwave policy, and consumers may add default-branch protection (not verified in this session: default-branch-protection).

Defense in depth: Shockwave still records a per-repository PR authorization and narrows every PR token to one repository and {contents: write, pull_requests: write}, so GitHub and Shockwave must both agree before a branch is pushed.

binding_checks.reader: The setup URL's installation_id is untrusted. Bind an installation to a consumer only if GET /user/installations with the signed-in user's user access token lists it (setup-url-spoofing, installations-rest).
binding_checks.pr_writer: The PR Writer has no sign-in callback. Bind its installation only if (1) GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation with the PR Writer's app JWT returns that installation for a repository the consumer marked for PRs, (2) its account matches the account of the consumer's verified Reader installation, and (3) the signature-verified installation.created webhook's sender is the signed-in GitHub user who requested PR authorization. This is a Shockwave design decision, not a GitHub-documented procedure (installation-token-generation, webhook-installation, webhook-signature).

sign_in.grants: Identity and a Shockwave session for one person.
sign_in.mechanism: Ishan's auth: 'Sign in with GitHub' through the Reader app's user authorization (web application flow with state and PKCE S256), or Ishan's own identity provider. The GitHub user access token is used only for GET /user (identity) and GET /user/installations (installation binding); it expires after 8 hours.
sign_in.stored_as: user identity (GitHub user id and login) and session; a user token, if kept, is stored encrypted
revoked_by: GitHub: Settings > Applications > Authorized GitHub Apps > Revoke (github_app_authorization webhook)
sign_in.effect_of_revocation: End the person's sessions and delete stored user tokens. Does not by itself change installations, repository selections or consents (separate authorizations held by the consumer organization); any further consent or PR-authorization change requires signing in again.

repository_access.grants: Shockwave may mint Reader installation tokens narrowed to one explicitly selected private repository with {contents: read, metadata: read} to fetch pinned snapshots.
repository_access.mechanism: GitHub: the Reader app installed with 'Only select repositories'. Shockwave: a RepositoryConnection per repository the signed-in consumer explicitly selected (a subset of the installation's repositories).
repository_access.granted_by: the consumer account or organization owner (installation) and a signed-in consumer user (selection)
revoked_by: removing the repository from the installation (installation_repositories removed)
repository_access.effect_of_revocation: Stop new snapshot fetches, scans, consumer-findings updates and provider-summary publication for the affected repositories; cancel queued jobs; delete stored snapshot archives.

analysis_consent.grants: Shockwave may scan the selected repositories' pinned snapshots for dependencies on the provider's API, analyze the provider's (here SIMULATED) change, run verification scenarios, prepare migration proposals, and publish the restricted provider summary.
analysis_consent.mechanism: Shockwave-only record; GitHub has no notion of it.
analysis_consent.granted_by: a signed-in consumer organization admin, after seeing the exact provider_visibility.allowed_fields
analysis_consent.stored_as: AnalysisConsent: consent_id, consumer_org_id, enrollment_id, api_project_id, repository_connection_ids, purposes, allow_model_processing (false: deterministic rules only), provider_summary_fields, consent text version, granted_by, granted_at, withdrawn_at
analysis_consent.effect_of_revocation: Stop new processing and publication for the covered repositories immediately; queued jobs fail their re-check; the provider summary shows only 'consent withdrawn'.

pr_write.grants: Push a NEW branch and open a migration pull request in one repository.
pr_write.mechanism: Both required: the PR Writer app installed with 'Only select repositories' on that repository, and a Shockwave per-repository PR authorization record. Tokens are narrowed to repository_ids=[that repository] and {contents: write, pull_requests: write}.
pr_write.granted_by: a consumer repository admin or account/organization owner (installation) and a signed-in consumer user (Shockwave authorization)
pr_write.stored_as: PR-writer installation record + PullRequestAuthorization per repository connection
does_not_grant: provider visibility of patches or pull requests
revoked_by: repository removed from the PR Writer installation
pr_write.effect_of_revocation: Cancel queued PR jobs; no new branches, pushes, pull requests or PR updates. Pull requests already opened stay under the consumer's control; Shockwave does not touch them again.

provider_visibility.rule: Default deny. The provider sees only allowed_fields, produced by an allowlist projection of consumer records, never by copying them. Everything in never_visible stays consumer-private at every step.

allowed_fields.consumer_org.display_name: the organization name the consumer agreed to show (fictional companies in this demo)
allowed_fields.enrollment.status: invited | accepted | connecting | connected | paused | access_revoked
allowed_fields.summary.impact_status: affected | not_affected_within_tested_scope | unresolved | not_run | access_revoked | consent_withdrawn
allowed_fields.summary.risk_counts_by_category: counts only, e.g. conversion / comparison / storage
allowed_fields.summary.verification_status_counts: counts of verified_regression / compatible_within_tested_scope / inconclusive / not_run
allowed_fields.summary.migration_readiness: none | prepared | validated_within_tested_scope (no patch content, no pull request link)
allowed_fields.summary.labels: SIMULATED change, deterministic rules (no LLM), LOCAL RUNNER DOUBLE, scanner FIXTURE

provider_visibility.aggregation: Counts are per consumer organization, never per repository, so repository names and counts are not revealed.

terminal_or_side_states.expired: invitation expired or was cancelled by the provider
terminal_or_side_states.paused: installation suspended, or repository made public: no processing until resolved and re-confirmed
terminal_or_side_states.access_revoked: installation deleted, repository removed, deselected, deleted or transferred

job_guards.rule: Authorization is re-checked immediately before each action, not only when a job is enqueued. A failed check cancels the job without side effects and records why. Lost or late webhooks are covered because the re-check asks GitHub (token minting) and Shockwave's records directly.

revocation_events.effect: All of the installation's RepositoryConnections become access_revoked; queued jobs are cancelled; stored snapshot archives are deleted; the provider summary shows access_revoked only.
Enrollment paused. On unsuspend, processing resumes only after a successful re-check (token minting, selection, consent); nothing is backfilled automatically.
Re-list GET /installation/repositories and revoke every RepositoryConnection no longer listed (repositories_removed is empty when selection changes from all to selected).
RepositoryConnection access_revoked; the new owner must onboard again.
RepositoryConnection paused: it is no longer a private repository; the consumer must re-confirm selection and consent.
RepositoryConnection access_revoked; queued jobs cancelled. The repository may stay in the GitHub installation, but Shockwave no longer uses it.
Covered repositories stop immediately; queued jobs fail their re-check; the provider summary shows consent_withdrawn only.
All PullRequestAuthorizations through this installation become revoked; queued PR jobs cancelled; analysis continues.
PR publication paused until unsuspended and re-checked.
Re-list the PR Writer installation's repositories; revoke PR authorization for every repository no longer listed.
No new branches, pushes or pull requests for the repository, even though the PR Writer may still be installed.
End the user's sessions and delete stored user tokens. Installations, selections and consents are separate authorizations and are not changed by this event alone.

non_revocation_events.effect: Not a grant of analysis: new repositories are listed as selectable but never selected or consented automatically.
Recorded only; never widens what Shockwave does without a separate consent or PR authorization.
Update the consumer-private full_name; connections are keyed by repository id.
